rows.h1: Keyword Research vs Prompt Research: The Future of SEO
text: Keyword Research vs Prompt Research: The Future of SEO
Keyword research finds what people search. Prompt research finds what people ask AI. Here's how both fit into a modern SEO content strategy in 2026.
Building One Workflow Instead of Two Separate Ones
Here are a few of the most important factors

Keyword research has been the foundation of content creation for search for around 2 decades. Users researched keywords with tools, entered seed terms, arranged by volume, chose targets, and formed content based on them. Though that method is still the same, it is no longer the only method used to create content for search. The reason you have witnessed a shift in traffic sources over the last year is due to the same reasons.

More and more of your audience members don’t browse search results by entering short keyword phrases. Users are opening one of the many AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google’s AI research mode, and “talking” to them. The nature of search is changing to the point where keyword research and planning is suddenly obsolete. Because of this, an auxiliary discipline has developed, Prompt Research.

The two research disciplines do not have to work against each other. The two research disciplines satisfy overlapping and distinct demands while creating and planning search content. This is why it is important to know how each of the two research disciplines works, and how they differ. Once you understand this, it is clear how the two can work together.

Keyword Research was a method used to find the short phrases and keywords searchers input into search engines. Keyword Research uses tools that analyze keyword competition and difficulty and related search terms, such as Google Keyword Planner, Ahrefs, or Semrush. Keyword Research is the precursor to the planning and creation of search content.

The whole model depends on aggregation. If you search “best running shoes for knee pain” in Google, there are likely millions of people searching the same term. A keyword research tool can provide insights into the search volume for that term, how competitive that search term is and synonyms that are closely related to that term. This was largely the framework for most of SEO strategy built over the last twenty years and is useful to understand demand at scale and to optimize pages for the classic, organic blue link search results.

Prompt research is the process of understanding the full, natural language questions people ask ChatGPT and convert them into similar formats to understand the questions being asked in other AI systems such as Perplexity or Google’s AI mode. Instead of “best running shoes knee pain,” the prompt may be, “I have mild knee pain from running, which shoes should I look at, and do I need custom orthotics too?”

The same underlying need with a totally new structure. Prompts tend to be longer, more specific and loaded with context, user constraints, their level of understanding, and even their budget or location. That additional information is actually useful because it shows that the person is way more advanced in the process and is not just browsing.

Due to the lack of volumetric data for the individual prompts that are asked a handful of times in slightly different forms, the type of AI research dealing with prompts works at a more abstract level. Rather than tracking the exact phrasing, this type of research looks at recurring questions and how AI systems answer those. This includes the sources cited, the brands suggested, and the content gaps that are leaving a brand completely out of those suggestions altogether.
Why is Prompt Research Increasing so Rapidly?

The most straightforward answer is that AI-assisted discovery is no longer a behavioral anomaly. The most recent industry data shows a considerable portion of consumers in the United States (some measure this as 35%+) are utilizing AI for product discovery compared to an even more dwindling segment of consumers using traditional search for product discovery. By the time a majority of buyers go to Google, they have already developed a shortlist elsewhere.

This fundamentally changes the shape of the funnel. If your content strategy relies solely on keywords, there is a high risk of optimizing for the latter half of the buyer's journey while completely ignoring the first half of the journey (the stage where AI tools are creating shortlists that your content needs to be a part of).

There’s a structural reason prompt research couldn’t grow from keyword research. Search volumes show what people ask, and content strategy has been built upon this foundation for the last twenty years. Now with AI search, users don’t input standardized keywords, they input prompts. Users input ad hoc prompts, and analyzing each prompt individually doesn’t scale. That’s why prompt research treats prompts as clusters and topics as opposed to isolated queries, just like how keyword tools treat search terms.
A good prompt research process has some steps that are more or less the same, even though the tools may differ.
Identify your target audiences and personas

Different people phrase requests with varying levels of competence, interest, and time. A beginner and an expert asking about the same thing will generate very different prompts, and you need to address both.
Utilize keyword research as a starting input

This is the merging of the two disciplines as opposed to the competing of the two disciplines. Your keyword list is a valid starting point for prompt research. Take a keyword and come up with three or four natural language questions someone would ask an AI about that keyword.

Some prompts matter more than others. Most informational prompts are useful for capturing visibility at the top of the funnel, but if you want to move the business forward, you want to know how AI begins comparing options, creates a shortlist, and makes recommendations (the middle and bottom of the funnel). Most importantly, you should know the prompts that trigger comparisons and create a shortlist or direct recommendation.
Examine how AI systems respond to those prompts

Go ahead and try the prompt yourself. See which sources get cited and which brands get named. See how the answer is framed. This will show you the winning answer format and how your potential answer content could fill the gap.

Rank tracking doesn't work here like it usually does. AI generated answers are more volatile than search results. The same prompt run on separate days can yield answers that are significantly different, with some studies showing variation of over 40% for the same prompt from one week to the next. Rather than trying to track a particular position, continuously check for your presence across those checks over time.

The most prudent thing to do is not choosing between keyword research and prompt research. Rather, both should be done for every single potential topic. Traditional keyword research becomes most valuable for finding a topic of focus, confirming that the topic is of interest to searchers, and capturing the demand for that topic. Immediately following, you should rephrase those keywords as natural language questions that people might ask their AI assistants about the same subject.

To help search engines understand what your article is about, you should write your content to align with the answer structure. These types of structures incorporate a clear direct response as the first or second sentence of new sections. Once you have adapted your content to new structures, you should include your short-tail keywords throughout the content, but avoid keyword stuffing. This allows you to optimize traditional SEO strategies. Once you have formatted your content to be primed for search, check the AI Overview and chatbot responses for your topic. You should then be aware of your competition's structure and the level of detail they are including. A fully optimized AI response is able to answer all short-tail and long-tail variations of a user's query.

By incorporating this strategy, a singular piece of content can fulfill audience engagement for both traditional search and AI Answer behavior. This offsets the previously required tradeoff that forced users to choose between the two.

A digital marketing training institute creates blog content about topics like updates in Google Ads and SEO, career paths in digital marketing, and more. Their keyword research shows that the term ”digital marketing course Bangalore” has some volume. This is a high-intent keyword and should be placed on its own page.

However, if we quickly perform keyword research for the same topic, we find that instead people are asking what digital marketing courses in Bangalore actually help you get placed in a job, or if it is worth taking a digital marketing certification, even with an engineering degree. These keywords are more specific and longer in length and reach a higher level of intent (or decision) than the keyword alone.

Building one page that targets the traditional SEO keyword and placing sections of that page, or closely linked companion pages, to each of the prompts and including a clear, direct answer near the beginning of the section. One content creation approach has much more potential to appear in Google's ranking and be used as an answer by AI assistants, instead of being optimized for only one function.

With keyword research, determining the highest priority items to target is as simple as ordering search volume. It is not as straightforward with AI writing prompts. More often than not, other factors end up being more important.

These will all require some judgement, but I've also found that it is less formulaic than keyword research. It is much easier to rank prompts and then go read through how the AI responds, and then work from there.
Shifting to AI search requires a different way of thinking about measurement. Here are some alternative methods:
Citation analysis: How many times does your domain or your brand get referenced when a target prompt is used repeatedly over several weeks?
Source quality analysis: Do AI systems include your content as a source for your target prompts, or do they still cite your competitors?
Traffic from AI systems: New tools in analytics separate traffic from ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc., and although the numbers are small, you should check this out too.
Behavior on pages built for prompt clusters: Once an AI answer brings a user to your site, your page engages them in the same way as traditional design.

Your existing approaches to traditional SEO are not replaced by these new methods. Rather, these methods offer new ways to understand visibilities that traditional keyword-based reporting cannot capture.
Considering prompt research a substitute for keyword research rather than a complement.
Focusing on prompt variability rather than prompts that elicit comparisons and recommendations.
Anticipating reliable volume or position data for prompts, as you would for keywords.
Writing content reflective of a keyword phrase that does not actually provide an answer to the more nuanced and complex question a prompt conveys.
Believing that the AI visibility check is a one-time proposition. Volatility of AI dictates that tracking must be ongoing.

During the last year, many software tools dedicated to prompt research have been developed. These tools have macro functions that assist in prompt and topic discovery, and micro functions that assist in tracking your brand's presence on prompts. Some tools, like Semrush's Prompt Research Tool and Similarweb's AI visibility, utilize large proprietary AI databases. Other tools, like SISTRIX and seoClarity, are focused on breaking prompt clusters and content briefs creation. Most of the established SEO tools have recently added at least an elementary version of this functionality. Before investing in a new tool, you should check if your existing tool has added this functionality recently.
Is prompt research replacing keyword research?

No. Keyword research helps you discover high demand search terms that people use. Prompt research shows the AI-driven format that people use when talking to the AI assistant. The best content strategies incorporate both keyword and prompt driven research.
Do I need special tools to do prompt research?

No, you can do prompt research on your own. You can take some of your top ranking keywords and rephrase them as questions to see how they answer in the assistant. Dedicated tools are more useful once you want to track your presence across many prompts at scale and to see changes over time.
How is 'ranking' measured for prompts if there's no position data?

In the absence of search results, prompt research does not measure ranking position. Instead, prompt research measures visibility based on the number of times a brand or article is referenced when a prompt is run repeatedly. Since answers to a prompt can vary dramatically, this needs to be checked frequently rather than just once.
Should small businesses waste their time on prompt research or is it better for large brands?

It is important for small businesses to do prompt research as well. Large brands can have more prompt resources as they have more content to cover informational areas. Often it is better for a smaller business to use prompt research to cover a narrow set of decision stage prompts that are directly related to their product offering rather than trying to cover informational areas.
What is the distinction between prompt research and GEO (generative engine optimization?

Prompt research is about the methodology used to find and prioritize the most worthwhile questions. On the other hand, GEO generally refers to the practice of tailoring content in such a way that generative systems are capable of recognizing, extracting, and citing it. In essence, prompt research is the foundation of a GEO strategy.
Will keyword volume data cease to be important?

It is unlikely that keyword volume data will become insignificant anytime in the future. Traditional search still exists, and as such, keyword volume reflects genuine, measurable demand in search. Traditional search has not been completely supplanted, so volume data is still one of the more trustworthy indicators so it is still worthwhile to use this data in prompt research, unlike disregarding it.

Keyword research continues to have its place and these ideas do not encourage the stopping of keyword research. What has changed is that keyword research is not as all encompassing as it once was. Prompt research covers the part of the funnel that keyword tools have no means of reaching - the questions people ask in a conversational context and in a manner that is rich in context before someone even thinks of going to a search engine. Brands that developed a workflow that integrates both are looking to maintain their presence in the results that are ranked, AI Overviews, and chatbot answers, as opposed to assuming AI-Driven search is the only way to discovery.

rows.h1: Google Ads Bidding Update 2026: What Marketers Must Know
text: Google Ads Bidding Update 2026: What Marketers Must Know
Google's August 17, 2026 bidding update is live. See what changed for Target CPA and Target ROAS campaigns, who's affected, and the exact steps to protect performance.
Which Campaigns Are Affected — and Which Aren't
• Search campaigns running Target CPA or Target ROAS
• Performance Max campaigns using target-based bidding
• Video reach and Video view campaigns
The Bid Target Adjustment Tool: Your Six-Week Head Start
What Digital Marketers Should Do This Week
What This Means for Performance Max and Demand Gen Specifically
In-house marketers and small business owners
Common Mistakes to Avoid Right Now
How This Fits Into Your Broader PPC Strategy

Today, August 17, 2026, is the enforcement date for one of the most consequential Google Ads bidding update rollouts in recent memory. If you manage Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen, or Travel campaigns on Target CPA or Target ROAS, your account is now operating under new rules — whether you prepared for them or not.

This Google Ads bidding update changes how budget-limited campaigns behave. For years, campaigns tagged "Limited by budget" have quietly overdelivered against their targets — a Target CPA set at ₹800 might have been landing conversions at ₹450. As of today, that gap closes. Google's Smart Bidding systems will optimize more literally toward the numbers you've actually typed into your account, not the efficiency they were unofficially delivering.

If that sounds like a small technical tweak, it isn't. For advertisers who never revisited their targets after initial setup, today's rollout can mean cost-per-acquisition doubling, ROAS targets suddenly binding instead of aspirational, and traffic reshuffling across Performance Max and Demand Gen channels. This guide breaks down exactly what's changing, who it affects, and the checklist every performance marketer should run through this week.
What Exactly Is the Google Ads Bidding Update?
At the center of this update is a single behavioral fix: how Target CPA and Target ROAS campaigns behave once they hit "Limited by budget" status.

Historically, when a campaign's daily budget capped how much Smart Bidding could spend, the system had room to cherry-pick only the cheapest, highest-probability conversions within that capped spend — which often meant actual performance beat the stated target by a wide margin. It felt like a bonus. In reality, it was an inconsistency in how the algorithm was applying targets under budget pressure.

From today onward, budget-limited campaigns using Target CPA, Target ROAS, or Target CPC (Demand Gen only) will optimize consistently toward the target you've set, even as your budget changes. Google has been explicit that this does not raise your budget ceiling — your daily and monthly spend caps are still respected. What changes is how efficiently the system uses that capped spend. The "accidental discount" many accounts were getting disappears.
Not every campaign type is touched by this Google Ads bidding update. Before auditing your account, it helps to know exactly where to look.

• Demand Gen campaigns using Target CPA, Target ROAS, or Target CPC • Travel campaigns on target-based strategies • Portfolio bid strategies and shared budgets (adjustments must be made at portfolio level)
• Display and Hotel campaigns (these already optimized this way, so nothing changes)

The single biggest qualifier is campaign status. This update only touches campaigns that are actively flagged "Limited by budget" in your account. If your Target CPA or Target ROAS campaigns have consistently had enough budget headroom, you likely won't notice any shift today.

Google's stated reasoning is consistency, not additional revenue extraction. In its own FAQ, Google frames the change as closing a gap between what advertisers ask for and what the system historically delivered under budget constraints. The company has also confirmed this bidding change will not, by itself, increase what you spend — your budget limits remain the ceiling.

That said, the practical effect for a lot of accounts will feel like a cost increase, because the "efficient" delivery many advertisers had gotten used to was never something Google formally guaranteed. If your Target CPA of ₹800 was quietly landing conversions around ₹450, that ₹450 was never the real target — it was budget-constrained overperformance. Today, the system starts closing that gap toward the number you actually set.

Google didn't spring this on advertisers without warning. Starting July 6, 2026, a Bid Target Adjustment Tool began rolling out inside affected Google Ads accounts, giving advertisers roughly six weeks to prepare before today's enforcement date.
The tool surfaces recent campaign performance directly next to your current target, making the gap visible in one screen, and offers three paths forward:
Apply Google's suggested target, aligned to your recent actual performance
Enter a custom target that reflects your real business economics or margin requirements
Leave the target unchanged and accept that performance will shift toward that original number

If you haven't seen this tool in your account, it may still be deploying — Google has said it will surface automatically in the relevant campaign settings pages as rollout continues. Importantly, Google has confirmed it will not auto-adjust your targets or budgets on your behalf. Whatever action you took (or didn't take) before today determines what your account looks like from here.
If you're managing paid media for a business, agency, or as a freelancer, here's the practical playbook now that the Google Ads bidding update is live.
Audit every campaign for "Limited by budget" status

Start in the Status column of your Google Ads campaigns view. Any Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen, or Travel campaign flagged this way, running on Target CPA or Target ROAS, is a candidate for today's shift. Don't skip accounts that haven't been actively managed recently — Google's notification trigger was broad, covering any campaign that was budget-limited at any point in the last 12 months.
Compare your stated target against actual recent performance

Pull the last 30–60 days of actual CPA or ROAS for each flagged campaign and set it next to the target currently configured. A wide gap tells you the campaign has been overdelivering, and that gap is what's closing starting today.
Decide: was the gap intentional or accidental?

This is the judgment call that matters most. Some advertisers set targets loosely on purpose, giving Smart Bidding room to explore and find efficiency — a deliberate strategy that this update quietly disables. Others simply never revisited a target set months or years ago during a testing phase. The right response is different for each: intentional headroom needs a new strategy, while a stale target just needs updating to reflect current margins.
Update targets to reflect real business economics

Rather than reverse-engineering a target from what the campaign used to deliver, calculate what CPA or ROAS your business can actually sustain based on current margins, average order value, and lead quality. Enter that number deliberately instead of leaving a legacy figure in place.
Consider Maximize Conversions or Maximize Conversion Value

For accounts uncomfortable committing to a hard CPA or ROAS target right now, switching to Maximize Conversions or Maximize Conversion Value lets the algorithm optimize within your set budget without being bound to a specific efficiency target. This is a reasonable interim move while you gather more data.
Give the algorithm time before reacting

Google's own guidance recommends waiting one to two full conversion cycles before drawing conclusions, and treating platform forecasts between August 17 and 31 with caution. If your typical customer takes a week to convert after clicking, judge performance on that timeline, not a bad first 48 hours.

Resist the urge to add data exclusions, impose bid limits, or make sweeping budget changes purely as a reaction to this update. These moves tend to introduce more volatility right when you need a stable baseline to measure the new behavior against.

Accounts running multi-channel strategies deserve extra attention. Because Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns often share budgets or compete for the same audience pools as Search and Shopping, a target that binds more strictly on one channel can shift how traffic gets distributed across the others. If your Performance Max campaign has historically been the account's efficiency workhorse — quietly landing cheap conversions inside a capped budget — expect that advantage to compress, and expect some reallocation of spend and volume toward channels that are less budget-constrained.

If you manage your own Google Ads account without a dedicated PPC specialist, this is the update most likely to catch you off guard. Legacy targets set during initial account setup and never revisited are exactly the campaigns exposed today. A single afternoon spent auditing targets against current margins is the highest-leverage task on your list this week.

Client communication matters as much as the technical fix here. Accounts that look stable today but shift meaningfully over the next two weeks need a heads-up before the client notices it themselves in a dashboard. Framing this proactively — as a platform-wide change affecting every advertiser, not an account-specific problem — protects trust.

Businesses with tight margins should treat this as a forcing function to revisit CPA and ROAS targets against real unit economics rather than historical platform behavior. A ROAS target that was comfortable at 4x but has quietly been performing at 5.5x was never a target you could rely on long-term — today's change just makes that visible.
A few reaction patterns are already showing up across PPC communities, and most of them make the transition harder rather than easier.

• Panic-cutting targets too aggressively. Dropping a Target CPA far below what your account's recent data supports doesn't force better performance — it just starves the campaign of eligible auctions and can crash volume entirely.

• Judging results from day one. Smart Bidding systems need a fresh learning period to adapt to how targets are now being enforced. A single day, or even a single week, of noisy data is not a verdict on how the update affects your account.
• Changing multiple levers at once. If you adjust the target, the budget, and the bid strategy in the same session, you won't be able to tell which change caused which effect once performance shifts.

• Ignoring campaigns that "look fine" today. A campaign that hasn't hit "Limited by budget" status this week can still be affected the moment seasonal demand or a promotion pushes it there. Build target reviews into a recurring monthly habit, not a one-time fix.

• Treating this as a one-account problem. This is a platform-wide change touching every advertiser running target-based bidding globally. If you manage multiple accounts, the audit checklist above needs to run against each one individually — the exposure looks different depending on each account's bidding history.

It's worth zooming out from the mechanics of this specific Google Ads bidding update to the bigger pattern it represents. Google's automated bidding systems have steadily moved toward rewarding advertisers who feed them accurate, well-tracked signals — clean conversion tracking, honest targets, and enough historical data for the algorithm to learn from — over advertisers who set-and-forget their campaigns.

This update reinforces that direction. Accounts with strong first-party conversion tracking, targets grounded in real margin data, and a habit of reviewing performance monthly are the ones least disrupted by changes like this. Accounts running on autopilot, with targets nobody has touched since launch, are the ones that get exposed every time Google tightens how its systems interpret the numbers advertisers give it.

For marketers building longer-term PPC skills, this is a useful moment to formalize a lightweight target-review cadence: a recurring monthly check of every campaign's budget-limited status against its actual delivered CPA or ROAS, rather than relying on Google to flag the gap for you next time.
Will this Google Ads bidding update increase my ad spend?

Not directly. Google has confirmed daily and monthly budget caps remain fully respected. What changes is how efficiently your capped spend gets used — meaning your cost per result may rise even though your budget ceiling doesn't.
Do I need to change anything if my campaigns aren't budget-limited?

No. This update only affects campaigns currently flagged "Limited by budget" and running Target CPA, Target ROAS, or Target CPC (Demand Gen only). Campaigns with sufficient budget headroom, or running Manual CPC, Target Impression Share, or Target CPM, are unaffected.
What if I missed the Bid Target Adjustment Tool notification?

You can still review and update your targets manually inside campaign settings today. The tool itself may still be visible for reference even after the enforcement date, showing recent performance next to your current target.
How long before I can judge the impact on my account?

Google recommends observing at least one to two full conversion cycles — and treating any forecasts or performance data from the two weeks immediately following August 17 with caution, since the system is still adapting.
Should I switch away from Target CPA or Target ROAS entirely?

Not automatically. If your targets are grounded in real performance data and reviewed regularly, staying on target-based bidding still gives you the most control over unit economics. Switching to Maximize Conversions or Maximize Conversion Value is a reasonable short-term move only if you genuinely don't yet have enough data to set a confident target — not a default reaction to this update.

Today's Google Ads bidding update doesn't make advertising more expensive on its own — it makes your targets accountable. Accounts that have kept Target CPA and Target ROAS numbers current, reviewed regularly against real business margins, will likely see little disruption. Accounts that set a target once and never looked back are the ones absorbing a real performance shift starting today.

The fix isn't complicated: audit which campaigns are budget-limited, compare targets against actual recent performance, decide honestly whether the gap was deliberate strategy or an oversight, and update your numbers to reflect what your business can genuinely sustain. Do that this week, give the algorithm a couple of conversion cycles to settle, and you'll be back to reading your Google Ads dashboard with confidence instead of confusion.

text: Digital Marketing Trends 2026: Complete Guide for Marketers
Discover the top digital marketing trends for 2026 — AI personalization, AEO/GEO, agentic AI, shoppable video, social commerce & more. Stay ahead with Acadvizen.
What This Means for Marketers in India
What This Means for Your Marketing Strategy
Common Mistakes Brands Make When Chasing Trends

Digital marketing today bears almost no resemblance to digital marketing from 2018. The search process has fundamentally altered. Instead of typing keywords into Google, people direct their search queries to AI assistants. Marketing platforms hire and fire staff on their own. The dynamic nature of such AI enables them to alter their bids and creatives on the fly. Digital marketers must know their customers across every marketing touchpoint, especially every channel, from the first impression to the post sale email.

This year, several trends will define how marketers do their work. The trends will include the impact of AI on content creation and search results, the fragmentation of users’ attention across distinct formats, the expansion of privacy regulations, and the erosion of users’ attention spans. The combination of these trends will result in the former best practices becoming obsolete.

This report analyzes the ten most significant trends that will define digital marketing in 2026. Rather than technical jargon, you will find summarized descriptions of each of the ten trends and the anticipated impact of each on this year’s digital marketing campaigns. If you are a business owner, brand marketing director, or are just starting your brand marketing career, you will want to put some of your marketing campaign efforts on hold until you have read this report.

Personalization is expected and AI is making it possible to do so at an individual level. Today's AI tools allow businesses to analyze how customers are browsing and what they are buying in order to make personalized recommendations. At the individual level, customers are more inclined to buy from companies that offer them relevant content and more likely to leave a company that is not offering them relevant content.

Marketers need to take this into consideration and start using AI to understand the customer interests more. Mass marketing campaign strategies are shifting to ones that use dynamic content, meaning the message adapts to each individual. Emails, landing pages, and even ads are produced in an AI-driven manner on an individual user basis.

At the product level, a user visiting the site for the first time compared to a user returning for the hundredth time are offered different tailored recommendations and content. The individual product page offers different product recommendations to different users.

Personalization will help your funnel process visitors. Even slight modifications will help your campaign a lot. Think about automating personalized email messages and recommendations. Retarget abandoned carts. It will help your campaign more than a general mass email would.

The marketing industry has exceeded using chatbots and content generators. Agentic AI can now execute marketing workflows with little to no human interaction. Real-time advertising, building and modifying marketing segmentation, or performing A/B testing are all marketing workflows. Now, marketers can tell these AI systems to perform these tasks, and the AI will then provide them performance-related updates.

Again, the Marketing job isn't eliminated. These AI systems will perform the tasks associated with low-level marketing execution. Instead, marketing professionals will now shift their focus to strategy, oversight, and interpreting the results. The execution tasks that were previously performed by marketing professionals will now be shifting to AI systems.

Consumers and marketers are very careful about letting AI make final purchase or budget decision on its own. The real world scenario is having AI doing the execution tasks, and marketing professionals need to approve any high stakes requests like significant changes to budget allocations, audience segments, or sensitive marketing messages.
AEO and GEO: Writing Content to Appear in AI Search Results

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) are the new kid on the optimization blocks. Much like traditional Search Engine Optimization, their goal is to optimize the content in a way that inspires AI-based assistance providers like Google's Bard, Microsoft's ChatGPT, and Perplexity to cite your content and provide your answers to end-users' queries.

Prioritize providing a clear, concise response to your given prompt early in your written piece. Do not answer the prompt at the end of your piece, or worse, bury it amongst a lengthy, unrelated introduction.
Utilize schema markup. This includes FAQ schema, Article schema and Local Business schema so AI systems and search engines can correctly process your content.
Competition for position on a search engine results page has evolved beyond keyword stuffing. Building topical authority relies on content depth for a subject, as opposed to multiple, isolated pages.
AI systems are progressively favoring sources that are verifiable, and citing sources with greater confidence. This means, facts, statistics and claims must be continually verified and up to date.

Brands who ignore this shift risk invisibility in a search landscape in which users no longer engage with sites beyond AI generated summaries. Traditional search result ranking has become less significant, as the source an AI system selects to cite has become increasingly significant.
Shoppable and Short-Form Video Dominate Attention

Consumers have a preference for short-form video content. Now, with the addition of shoppable video, set to dominate by 2026, purchases can be made by video consumers. Shoppable video content is video content that provides the consumer a direct purchasing option, without the need to leave the content. As a result, video, as a brand awareness and product discovery tool, will become a brand revenue tool. The gap that previously existed between brand awareness, product discovery and purchasing will be eliminated with a single consumer action.

Connected TV (CTV) similarly evolved from strictly brand-centric advertising to measurable direct response advertising to the degree that television advertising can attribute sales to a television advertisement. Small businesses receive more level playing field opportunities, as high advertising production value is replaced by resolute target specific, timely help messages. An example is a relevant, short mobile filmed video that outperforms a slick expensive advertising campaign that requires several weeks to execute.

Buying social ads to sell direct on social applications (without a redirect) is beyond Instagram. Selling direct on social applications is growing across other platforms and retail media networks with closed-loop measurement advertising on retailer platforms and marketplaces.

For brands, product catalogs, checkout, and customer service must be embedded within social applications. Traditional social applications have purely been used as an advertising channel and a sales loss opportunity has been created.
From Traditional Influencer Deals to Creator Partnerships

A new level of collaboration is occurring within the influencer economy. Sponsored Posts have been replaced with extended partnerships that provide the creator deep involvement in the operating and strategic aspects of the partnership. This collaboration provides a measurable level of product trust over broad product reach.

Journal recommendations become commercials, and audiences suss them out. Mast is more effective. Micro and niche creators have smaller audiences, but those audiences are specific and engaged. Those creators cash out advertisement deals, unlike celebrity deals that have a large but dispersed audience.

First-party data will be marketing's most valuable asset with the exit of third-party cookies and the global increase of privacy regulations. Organizations are spending money to build direct relationships with customers to gather data rather than relying on advertising to do it for them. First-party data will be marketing's most important competitive advantage.

Building a direct customer relationship is also the foundation of a new measurement paradigm. As tracking becomes more regulated, customer interactions will be modeled and segmented aggregations will be used instead of tracking customers at an individual level.
Immersive Content: AR, VR, and Interactive Experiences

The days of AR and VR being used only in high priced advertising campaigns are over. Users across multiple industries can now build AR applications that allow for virtual product sampling. Furniture and automotive companies can use interactive product configuration to create custom products.
Interactive content engages users longer than static content. Configurators and AR applications ask the user to engage in the experience, unlike static content, which is one directional.
Cross-Channel Measurement and Marketing Mix Modeling

Advertising spans search, social, video, TV, connected TV, and retail media networks. Hardly easier, it has become more difficult to understand what is actually working. However, Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) is experiencing greater investment as marketeers move away from attribution models and recognize that people buy following a series of complex interactions and not a single, last-touch interaction.

Predictive forecasting is a related concern. A large percentage of marketers consider the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models prior to a campaign launch to determine an expected course of campaign performance to be of more importance than post campaign performance evaluation after the budget has been spent.

More AI-based content increases audience preference for content that is human and authentic. Content that includes messaging and points of view that cannot be AI generated commands an audience. Brands that use AI to mass content production at scale are paired with a human perspective are outperforming those that only use AI to mass content production.

By 2026, many will recognize authenticity as a competitive advantage. Inclusivity, diversity, and real customer stories will dominate the balance of the highly digital campaign trends and the most human of these trends.

The trends impact the marketing activities carried out by businesses and marketers in India, including those in Bengaluru, one of the fast-growing cities. The impact is seen in the consumption of short-form mobile videos and the availability of regional content in local vernacular and the predominance of search queries on mobile. Internet usage on smartphones is more dominant than internet usage on desktop computers.

Businesses that leverage AI-search-ready content, Google Business Profile optimization, and LocalBusiness schema will be able to cater to both traditional local search and to local search that is answered by AI assistants. Optimization of social media, AI-assisted content creation, and analytics is crucial for new workers as organizations are hiring staff that can work alongside these platforms without requiring any additional training.

A variety of trends impact the marketing strategies of organizations in a variety of different ways. Organizations should not follow a variety of trends. Rather, they should select a few trends that will best serve their business and implement those trends well. Some organizations may choose to focus on the AI-based search, while others may choose to develop a first-party data strategy or shift their advertising budget to shoppable videos.

All ten trends demonstrate marketing becoming increasingly personal and automated. The automation of marketing means that the strategy and thought behind the marketing is crucial. Understanding your audience and data, and getting the correct positioning in the market is the new marketing strategy, and is more crucial than ever before. To prioritize, look at what trend affects your customer in how your customer discovers and chooses your brand. Once you know that, you can adjust the rest.

There are many issues that brands run into as they chase marketing trends without a correct strategy. The most obvious issue is brands adopting AI technology to do marketing for them, by having AI write their content. This has a negative effect by eroding trust. Some other issues that brands have are even if they are spending money on the latest marketing channels, such as shoppable video, they do not ensure their target customer uses that marketing channel. Having a first-party data collection system and never actually using that data is pointless. Brands tend to badly optimize their websites and marketing content for search engine bots instead of for people.

AI’s marketing answers become more popular than organic content, and brands try to keep up with this new marketing trend by spending all of their marketing budget on things that will become stale and useless.

The businesses that will outperform most of their competitors in 2026 aren't necessarily utilizing the largest number of marketing tools. These forward-thinking businesses have adopted a strategy of identifying trends aligned with their buyer's behavior and building the skills to execute on these trends consistently (not sporadically) rather than the large number of tools available.
What is the biggest digital marketing trend in 2026?

The top trend for 2026 is the increased use of AI in the creation and optimization of digital marketing campaigns. AI will impact digital marketing across all channels: from the bid on ad placements, to the creation of digital marketing content, to the segmentation of marketing campaigns.
What is AEO and GEO in digital marketing?

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) are terms used to describe techniques for creating content to enable AI and ChatGPT to include your content when answering a search query.
Is traditional SEO still relevant in 2026?
Yes. Traditional SEO best practices coupled with Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) are needed to create a robust digital marketing strategy.
How can beginners start a career in digital marketing in 2026?

The best path to a digital marketing career is to complete a rigorous digital marketing course focused on AI. Digital marketing employers have shifted to a preference for digital marketing experience rather than digital marketing coursework.
Do small businesses need to adopt all these trends at once?

Small businesses do not need to adopt all of these trends at the same time. Small businesses have the most success by choosing a couple of trends, the ones that are most relevant to where their customers' time and attention are, and doing exceptionally well with those. After that, they expand little by little, as opposed to a small business spreading their resources on every new trending channel.

At Acadvizen, our Digital Marketing and AI-based Digital Marketing modules have been built around these changes, including AEO/GEO-centric content strategies and paid advertising along with a range of services all powered by AI. Live projects are the building blocks of everything we teach. At our centers in Jayanagar, Bengaluru, we welcome aspiring students and working professionals alike.

rows.h1: Zero-Click SEO: Google AI Overviews & Snippets
text: Zero-Click SEO: Google AI Overviews & Snippets
Learn how to optimize for zero-click searches and Google AI Overviews. Discover proven SEO strategies to increase organic traffic and improve search visibility in 2026.
The Business Impact: Lost Clicks, New Opportunities
Zero Click Search SEO: Core Strategies to Increase Organic Traffic
Search engines and AI systems favor content that is easy to parse. Use
Traditional CTR and session metrics understate value. Track
Advanced Tactics for Sustained Traffic Growth

Zero-click searches have transformed organic search. A growing majority of Google queries now end without a single click to an external website. Users get answers directly on the results page through featured snippets, People Also Ask boxes, knowledge panels, and especially Google AI Overviews. For content creators and businesses that rely on organic traffic, this shift feels like a crisis. Impressions rise while clicks fall. Rankings that once delivered steady visitors now deliver brand mentions instead of sessions.

This is not temporary. Zero-click behavior has climbed steadily for years and accelerated sharply with the broad rollout of AI Overviews. The good news is that smart Zero Click Search SEO still drives results. Brands that optimize for visibility inside the SERP—winning featured snippets, earning citations in Google AI Overviews, and strengthening topical authority—can protect and even grow traffic, brand searches, and conversions. This guide explains what zero-click searches are, why they matter, how Google AI Overviews changed the game, and the practical strategies that increase organic traffic in this new landscape.

A zero-click search occurs when a user types a query into Google (or another search engine), receives a satisfactory answer on the results page itself, and leaves without clicking any blue link. The answer may come from a featured snippet (often called Position Zero), an AI Overview summary, a knowledge panel, a local pack, a People Also Ask expansion, or even Google’s own properties.

Historically, roughly half of searches ended without a click. By 2024 that figure sat near 58–60 percent in the United States. By early 2026 many studies placed the overall rate between 65 and 68 percent, with mobile searches running higher (often above 70 percent). Informational queries show the highest zero-click rates—frequently 75–80 percent—while transactional queries remain lower. When an AI Overview appears, the zero-click rate jumps further, often reaching 80–83 percent.

These numbers come from large-scale clickstream analyses and controlled studies. They confirm what many site owners already see in Google Search Console: impressions climb, average position stays strong, yet clicks and CTR decline. The “Great Decoupling” of impressions from clicks is now the default experience for informational content.
Why Zero-Click Searches Are Rising: The Role of Google AI Overviews

Google has spent more than a decade adding features that answer questions without requiring a click. Featured snippets, knowledge graphs, and rich results all contributed. Google AI Overviews accelerated the trend dramatically after their wider rollout in 2024 and continued expansion through 2025–2026.

AI Overviews generate concise, multi-source summaries at the top of the results page. They appear most often for longer, question-based, and informational queries. Coverage varies by vertical—health, how-to, and educational topics see the highest rates—but the overall footprint keeps expanding. When an AI Overview is present, traditional organic CTR typically drops 30–60 percent depending on the study and query type. Position-one CTR can fall from the high twenties into the low twenties or lower. Users who see the summary are also more likely to end their session on Google entirely.

Featured snippets still matter, but AI Overviews often sit above them or replace them. People Also Ask boxes continue to expand on-page. Local packs and knowledge panels capture local and branded intent. Together these features keep more users inside Google’s ecosystem.

The impact is uneven. Sites heavy in pure informational content (definitions, basic how-tos, listicles that add little original insight) feel the sharpest declines. Brands that already rank well and produce distinctive, experience-backed content fare better. Importantly, being cited inside an AI Overview often correlates with higher subsequent branded searches and, in some analyses, better relative performance on the remaining clicks. Visibility still has value even when the immediate click does not arrive.

Organic traffic declines of 15–25 percent (and higher in some verticals) have been widely reported since AI Overviews scaled. News and pure informational publishers have seen especially steep drops. Yet the story is not pure loss.

Brand mentions inside AI Overviews and featured snippets build awareness and trust. Users who later search the brand name convert at higher rates. Downstream metrics—branded search volume, direct traffic, email sign-ups, and assisted conversions—can offset some of the pure-click decline. Sites that treat zero-click visibility as a top-of-funnel awareness channel rather than a pure traffic play adapt more successfully.
The strategic shift is clear: traditional ranking for “10 blue links” is no longer enough. Success now requires ranking and being selected for the answer surfaces that users actually consume.

Winning in a zero-click world means optimizing for the features that create zero-click experiences while still capturing the remaining clicks and converting the brand equity they generate. Here are the highest-leverage approaches.

Featured snippets remain one of the most reliable ways to claim Position Zero. Google still extracts them from pages that already rank on the first page (nearly all snippets come from positions 1–10). The format that matches the query type wins:
Paragraph snippets (definitions, “what is,” “why”) work best with a clear 40–60-word answer placed immediately after a question-style H2 or H3.
List snippets (how-to, steps, “ways to,” “best”) prefer ordered or unordered lists of 4–8 concise items.
Table snippets (comparisons, pricing, specs) need clean HTML tables with clear headers.

Identify opportunities by filtering Google Search Console queries that already rank in positions 1–10 and contain question modifiers (“what,” “how,” “why,” “best,” “vs”). Manually check which of those queries already show a snippet.
Mirror the exact user question in an H2 or H3.
Lead with the direct answer in the first 40–60 words under that heading—no fluff or preamble.
Follow with supporting detail, examples, and original insight so the page remains valuable if the user does click.
Use proper HTML lists and tables; avoid image-only or JavaScript-rendered content for the answer block.
Add FAQ or HowTo schema where relevant.

Many sites that already rank well can capture the snippet simply by restructuring existing content. Capturing the snippet often increases overall visibility and can still drive meaningful clicks when the answer is incomplete or the user wants more depth.
Optimize for Google AI Overviews Citations

AI Overviews synthesize information from multiple sources. Being one of those sources delivers high-visibility brand exposure even if the click-through rate on the citation itself is low (often around 1 percent in some studies). The pages that get cited tend to:
Demonstrate clear expertise, experience, authoritativeness, and trustworthiness (E-E-A-T).
Answer the query and related sub-questions comprehensively.
Contain unique data, original research, first-hand experience, or distinctive frameworks that AI systems cannot easily reconstruct from generic sources.
Use clear structure, headings, and schema that help machines parse the content.
Publish content that adds genuine information gain—primary data, case studies, proprietary methods, or expert commentary.
Cover the full topic cluster so the page (or site) becomes the natural source for related questions.
Keep content fresh and accurate; outdated statistics reduce trust signals.
Implement Article, FAQPage, HowTo, and Organization schema.
Build topical authority through content clusters rather than isolated pages.
Earn high-quality backlinks and brand mentions that reinforce entity recognition.
Monitor AI Overview presence for your priority keywords and note which domains are cited. Aim to become one of those sources by producing superior, more complete, or more current answers.
Target People Also Ask and Related Questions

PAA boxes expand on the page and keep users engaged without leaving Google. Answering multiple related questions on a single page increases the chance of appearing in several PAA slots and strengthens the page’s overall authority for the topic. Structure each answer with its own clear heading and concise response (2–4 sentences) followed by deeper explanation.
Tables and lists where they aid clarity.
Comprehensive schema markup (FAQ, HowTo, Article, Organization, Product, etc.) implemented in a crawlable way (preferably server-side or static).
Schema does not guarantee a feature, but it removes ambiguity and improves eligibility.
Shift Toward Higher-Intent and Brand-Building Content
Pure top-of-funnel informational content faces the highest zero-click rates. Balance the content mix:
Create more commercial-investigation and transactional content that still ranks but faces lower AI Overview pressure.
Develop proprietary tools, calculators, templates, or data reports that users must visit the site to use.
Build strong brand presence so that even when users see your name in an AI Overview they later search for you directly.
Invest in email lists, communities, and owned channels that reduce dependence on Google referrals.
Measure What Matters in a Zero-Click World
Impression share and SERP feature ownership (featured snippets, AI Overview citations, PAA).
Share of voice inside AI Overviews for priority topics.
Engagement and conversion rates on the traffic that does click through (often higher quality).
Compare periods before and after major AI Overview expansions in your niche to quantify the true impact and the recovery from optimization work.

Build topical authority systematically. Map the core topics and related subtopics in your niche, then create comprehensive cluster content that interlinks naturally. AI systems prefer coherent, authoritative sources over fragmented pages.

Prioritize original research and first-hand experience. Content that merely rephrases what already exists across the web is easy for AI to summarize and less likely to earn distinctive citations. Unique data, experiments, interviews, or case studies create information gain that machines still need to reference.
Optimize for voice and multi-modal search. Featured snippets and concise answer blocks frequently feed voice assistants. Clear, spoken-language answers improve eligibility.

Monitor competitor SERP features and reverse-engineer winning formats. Tools that surface SERP feature data make this efficient. When a competitor holds a valuable snippet or citation, improve upon their answer with better structure, depth, or freshness.

Diversify traffic sources. While perfecting Zero Click Search SEO, expand presence on platforms where users still click or engage deeply—YouTube, LinkedIn, newsletters, communities, and emerging AI chat interfaces that surface sources.
Chasing every featured snippet opportunity without first ranking on page one.
Writing long, rambling introductions before the direct answer.
Treating AI Overviews as pure loss instead of a brand-visibility channel.
Ignoring mobile experience (zero-click rates are higher on mobile).
Measuring success solely by organic sessions while ignoring branded search and assisted metrics.
Producing thin or duplicated content that adds no unique value.

Zero-click searches will continue. Google’s incentives align with keeping users on its properties and delivering fast answers. AI Overviews and future iterations will expand. At the same time, users still click when the on-page answer is incomplete, when they need depth, tools, transactions, or community, and when brand trust is high.

The winners will be those who treat the SERP itself as a primary marketing surface. They will structure content for extraction, build genuine expertise that machines and humans both recognize, and convert the visibility they earn into owned relationships and higher-intent traffic.

Zero Click Search SEO is not about fighting the trend. It is about adapting to it—claiming the answer boxes, earning the citations, strengthening the brand, and capturing the clicks that remain. Sites that execute these strategies consistently can increase organic traffic relative to competitors even as the overall click rate declines. The traffic that arrives will often be more intentional and more valuable.

Start with an audit of your top informational pages. Restructure the highest-opportunity ones for featured snippets. Add the schema and depth that improve AI Overview eligibility. Track the new metrics. Iterate. In a world where most searches produce no click, the brands that still appear prominently—and convert the attention they receive—will own the next era of organic growth.

Zero-click searches occur when users find the information they need directly on the search results page without clicking on a website. This often happens through AI Overviews, featured snippets, knowledge panels, and local packs.
Zero-click searches are growing because Google and other search engines provide instant answers using AI, featured snippets, and rich search results, allowing users to get information more quickly.
How do zero-click searches affect website traffic?
Zero-click searches can reduce click-through rates for some keywords. However, optimizing for AI search features and rich results can improve brand visibility and attract higher-quality visitors.
Can I still increase organic traffic with zero-click searches?

Yes. You can increase organic traffic by targeting long-tail keywords, creating in-depth content, optimizing for featured snippets, implementing schema markup, and publishing content that answers user intent.
What is the difference between zero-click searches and Google AI Overviews?
Zero-click searches refer to any search where users don't click a result. Google AI Overviews are one type of zero-click experience that uses artificial intelligence to generate summarized answers.
How can I optimize my content for zero-click searches?
Use clear headings, answer common questions directly, add FAQ and How-To schema, optimize for featured snippets, improve page speed, and publish trustworthy, high-quality content.
What are featured snippets, and why are they important?
Featured snippets are highlighted answer boxes displayed at the top of Google search results. They increase your content's visibility and can establish your website as a trusted source.
Does schema markup help with zero-click searches?
Yes. Schema markup helps search engines understand your content better and can improve your chances of appearing in rich results, FAQs, featured snippets, and AI-generated search experiences.
Are zero-click searches bad for SEO?
No. While they may reduce clicks for some informational queries, they also create opportunities to increase brand awareness, build authority, and appear in AI-powered search features.
What is the future of zero-click searches?

Zero-click searches are expected to become even more common as AI-powered search evolves. Businesses that focus on helpful content, E-E-A-T, structured data, and user experience will be better positioned to succeed.

Learn how to choose the right affiliate marketing program as a beginner. Compare Amazon Associates, ClickBank, and niche affiliate programs to maximize your earnings.

How to Choose the Right Program: A Simple Framework
Use this checklist when evaluating any affiliate program
FAQ: Best Affiliate Programs for Beginners

Affiliate marketing is one of the most accessible ways for beginners to earn online income. You promote products or services, and when someone buys through your unique link, you earn a commission—no inventory, no customer service, and often no upfront cost.

The key challenge for newcomers is choosing the right program. Not every affiliate offer fits a beginner. Some pay low commissions, have strict approval rules, or require large audiences. Others are beginner-friendly with easy approval, solid tracking, and products people actually want.

This guide walks you through how to evaluate affiliate programs and compares three popular options: Amazon Associates, ClickBank, and niche affiliate networks. By the end, you’ll know which path makes the most sense for your situation.
Many new affiliates jump into the first program they find and then struggle. Common beginner mistakes include:
Amazon Associates is often the first program beginners join—and for good reason.

Best for: Bloggers, YouTubers, and content creators who already talk about products people buy on Amazon (tech, books, home, beauty, etc.). It works well when you create helpful reviews, comparisons, or “best of” lists.
Beginner tip: Focus on higher-commission categories (e.g., Amazon devices, certain fashion or beauty items) and combine Amazon links with higher-paying offers from other networks when possible.
ClickBank is a long-standing marketplace focused mainly on digital products (info products, software, health & wellness, make-money offers, etc.).
Best for: Affiliates who create content around personal development, health, relationships, or online business and who are comfortable promoting digital products.
Beginner tip: Start with products that have solid gravity scores and positive reviews. Always test the sales funnel yourself before promoting.

Niche affiliate networks (or specialized platforms) focus on specific industries—fashion, software/SaaS, outdoor gear, finance, beauty, pet products, etc. Examples include ShareASale, CJ Affiliate, Impact, Awin, and smaller vertical networks.
Best for: Affiliates who have (or plan to build) a focused niche site or audience. Once approved, these programs often outperform general marketplaces long-term.
Beginner tip: Apply to 3–5 relevant networks early. Many approve smaller sites if your content is helpful and your traffic is genuine. Start with networks known to be friendlier to new publishers.
Audience match – Does the product solve a problem your readers/viewers actually have?
Commission & cookie – Is the payout worth the effort? How long does the cookie last?
Approval & requirements – Can a beginner get in?
Tracking & support – Is the dashboard clear? Is support responsive?
Reputation – Do other affiliates speak positively about payments and product quality?
Your content style – Reviews, tutorials, comparisons, email sequences, or social posts?

Most successful beginners start with Amazon Associates for easy wins and broad product access, add ClickBank (or similar) for higher digital commissions in matching niches, and gradually layer in niche networks as their site and authority grow.
Create helpful content first (don’t lead with “buy this”).
Diversify—don’t rely on a single program.
Focus on one niche long enough to build trust and rankings.
Affiliate marketing rewards consistency more than chasing the highest commission rate. Choose programs that fit your audience and content style, then create genuine value around those products.
Q: What is the best affiliate program for complete beginners?
A: Amazon Associates is usually the easiest starting point because approval is simple and the product range is massive. Many beginners pair it with one higher-paying network later.
Q: Is ClickBank good for beginners?
A: Yes, if your niche involves digital products (courses, software, health info, etc.). Commissions are higher, but you need to carefully select quality offers.
Q: Should I join multiple affiliate networks?
A: Yes. Most experienced affiliates use Amazon + one or two niche networks. Diversifying reduces risk if one program changes terms.
Q: How much can a beginner realistically earn?
A: Results vary widely. Some earn their first $100–500 within a few months with consistent content; others take longer. Focus on building useful content rather than quick income.
Q: Do I need a website to start affiliate marketing?
A: A website gives you more control and better long-term results, but you can also start on YouTube, social media, or email. Most serious programs prefer (or require) a site eventually.
Q: What’s the biggest mistake beginners make with affiliate programs?
A: Promoting products just because the commission is high instead of choosing products their audience actually needs and trusts.

Choosing the right affiliate marketing program as a beginner doesn’t have to be complicated. Start with easy, trusted platforms like Amazon Associates, explore higher-commission options such as ClickBank when they fit your niche, and expand into specialized networks as you grow. Prioritize audience value, clear tracking, and sustainable commissions—and you’ll build a much stronger foundation than chasing the “highest paying” offer of the week.
